annotations.description: Mycoloth without any creatures to devour enters as a vanilla 4/4 that generates 0 Saproling tokens per upkeep, making it very underwhelming for its 5 mana cost. Jarad, Golgari Lich Lord was castable ({B}{B}{G}{G} available from Golgari Rot Farm + Swamp + 2 Forests) and would have been a 3/3 with a powerful sacrifice ability that synergizes with the deck's graveyard theme, plus it grows as more creatures enter the graveyard.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mycoloth with no creatures to devour, resulting in a vanilla 4/4 with no +1/+1 counters and zero token generation.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Jarad, Golgari Lich Lord, which provides a sacrifice outlet, a relevant drain ability, and graveyard recursion, offering much more strategic value.

annotations.description: Cast Jarad (a 3/3 with limited utility due to no sacrifice fodder) over Mycoloth (a 4/4 that generates saproling tokens each upkeep). The reasoning incorrectly states Mycoloth isn't available/castable, but it's in hand and castable with the available mana ({3}{G}{G} from 6 available mana via Golgari Rot Farm producing 2). Mycoloth's token generation provides much better board development even without devour targets.
annotations.betterLine: Play a Forest from hand, then cast Mycoloth. Even as a base 4/4, it generates saproling tokens each upkeep, building a board presence that synergizes with future Jarad plays.

annotations.description: Mycoloth without any creatures to sacrifice to Devour is just a vanilla 4/4 with no meaningful ability. The only creature available to devour is Jarad (the commander), which would be a terrible sacrifice. Meanwhile, Butcher of Malakir (5/4 flyer with forced sacrifice trigger) was castable for exactly 7 mana (5BB) with the available lands, and would have been far more impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mycoloth as a vanilla 4/4 with no Devour targets (or only Jarad to sacrifice).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Butcher of Malakir (5BB) using Golgari Rot Farm + Swamp for BB and remaining lands for 5 generic. A 5/4 flyer with a powerful edict effect on creature death synergizes perfectly with Jarad's sacrifice ability.

annotations.description: Jarad is a 3/3 (base 2/2 + 1 from Cloudthresher in graveyard) that could attack any opponent for likely unblocked damage. Most opponents either have no blockers (Qwen3L), only flyers that can't block ground (GLM47's Tegwyll and Bladecrafter, Haiku's Sigarda), or small ground creatures that would trade poorly. Jarad's sacrifice ability ({1}{B}{G}) doesn't require him to be untapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with any creatures, passing up free combat damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Jarad into an opponent with no good ground blockers (like Qwen3L Vorthos with only lands, or GLM47 Gramps whose creatures all have flying) for 3 free damage.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps declined to attack with two evasive Faeries (Faerie Bladecrafter 2/2 flying and Nettling Nuisance 3/1 flying) when no opponent has untapped flying blockers. Attacking would deal 5 damage, put a +1/+1 counter on Faerie Bladecrafter, AND create a goaded 4/2 Pirate token for the damaged player that can't block and must attack someone other than Gramps - extremely valuable when at 9 life since it redirects aggression. All of Gramps' lands are tapped so there's no mana to hold up anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Faerie Bladecrafter and Nettling Nuisance at the most threatening opponent (likely Gem25F Libby who has Mycoloth generating tokens). This gains a +1/+1 counter on Bladecrafter, deals 5 damage, and creates a goaded 4/2 Pirate that must attack someone other than Gramps.

annotations.description: Failed to play the Forest from hand before casting Butcher of Malakir. Even though the extra mana wouldn't change the plays available this turn, missing a land drop is always suboptimal - it provides information hiding and ensures you don't forget later, and the extra mana could matter on future turns if something happens at instant speed.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Butcher of Malakir without first playing the Forest from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play the Forest from hand first, then cast Butcher of Malakir.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Putrefy on Runic Armasaur in response to Bonehoard on the stack, so the Armasaur is in the graveyard when Bonehoard resolves, making the Germ a 5/5 instead of 4/4.
